newsitem.title: UK: UK gas flexibility mechanism sells heavily at weekend.
newsitem.headline: UK gas flexibility mechanism sells heavily at weekend.

text.p: The flexibility mechanism, the trading system used in Britain to keep daily gas supply and demand in balance, sold substantial volumes of gas over the weekend, reflecting unexpectedly low demand.

British Gas pipeline arm TransCo, which operates the flexibility mechanism, said on Monday that the system had sold 58,305,322 kilowatt hours (around 1.989 million therms) of gas on Friday in four lots, at an average 0.4842 p/kWh (around 14.19 pence a therm).
On Saturday, there was a further system sell of 119,909,552 kWh (around 4.091 million therms) in eleven lots at an average 0.4625 p/kWh (around 13.554 pence a therm).
And on Sunday, nine lots totalling 88,815,153 kWh (around 3.03 million therms) were sold at an average price of 0.4073 p/kWh, or around 11.937 pence a therm.
Prices on the flexibility mechanism have been highly volatile in recent weeks, with trade seen as high as 58 pence a therm on November 19.

But there have been more system sells than buys since then, and the mild recent weather has kept flexibility prices below current spot prices. December gas was discussed between 18.50/19.50 pence a therm on Monday afternoon on the spot market, traders said, with very prompt gas worth more than this.
